title: How Black Holes Form: The Science Explained
meta_description: Learn how massive stellar cores collapse into black holes, how supermassive black holes grow, and which formation pathways remain uncertain.
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: A black hole forms when enough mass becomes concentrated within a region from which escape paths, including those for light, cannot reach distant observers.
Many stellar-mass black holes form when the core of a massive star collapses after its nuclear fuel can no longer support it against gravity, though outcomes depend on stellar properties.
Supermassive black holes reside in many galactic centres, but the origin of their earliest seeds and the pathways by which they grew remain unsettled.
Black holes are not cosmic vacuum cleaners: far away, their gravity behaves like that of any object with the same mass; the event horizon marks the boundary beyond which signals cannot escape.
